summary: Change 1.0.6.8.4 expands Vanilla gameplay and world events, PvP systems, Playerbot support, dungeon automation and server stability.  Quest and world improvements include Ahn'Qiraj raid quest credit, Twin Emperors immunities, the Gizelton Caravan, Wild Hearts, Blackrock Depths maintenance and Twilight Cultist changes in Silithus.  Elemental Invasions now have a calendar-based monthly schedule: they begin on the first day of each month, last five full days and are designed to recover correctly after server restarts. The Resource Hub provides a matching countdown to the next invasion or the end of the current event. Live event validation and timezone synchronisation remain outstanding.  PvP additions include forced faction PvP zones, Honor Overflow and fortnightly Honor resets. Optional expansion-aware Meeting Stone and Battleground queueing rules recreate earlier expansion restrictions; the Battleground server-side restriction remains disabled by default pending testing.  Playerbots and Dungeon Clear have received updates to equipment selection, raid behaviour, dungeon routes, threat management, Battleground participation, encounters and automated testing.  Naxxramas Core expands class mechanics, Playerbot consumable preparation, talent management and optional Mage movement customisation. Systems awaiting compilation or in-game validation retain their development status.  N Addon Collection v1.0.0 provides five server-focused addons in one download. Dungeon Journal has expanded Vanilla coverage, the Naxxramas MultiBot Chatless fork adds consumable controls, N Classic Battlegrounds adapts the PvP interface and Naxxramas Loot Ledger remains in development.  Future-progression content, Resource Hub navigation, addon documentation and the technical foundations of AzerothCore have also been improved. The existing raid and expansion unlock schedule is unchanged.

CHANGE 1.0.6.8.4 — SERVER UPDATE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Change 1.0.6.8.4 brings together improvements to Vanilla quests and encounters, recurring world events, PvP and Honor systems, Playerbots, Dungeon Clear, Naxxramas Core and the Naxxramas Resource Hub.

The update introduces a calendar-based monthly Elemental Invasions schedule, expansion-aware Meeting Stone and Battleground options, further class and talent integration, dungeon automation improvements and server stability work.

N Addon Collection v1.0.0 provides five Naxxramas-focused addons in one official download, alongside new releases and improvements to individual addons.

Optional features that are disabled by default or still awaiting compilation and live testing are identified in their respective sections.

# QUESTS, WORLD & VANILLA CONTENT:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

# Ahn'Qiraj War — Raid Quest Credit

Several custom Ahn'Qiraj War event quests have received an important correction.

Previously, players completing certain war-event objectives while participating in a raid group could fail to receive the appropriate kill credit.

The affected quests include:

- Chaos and Destruction — Lieutenant General Nokhor.
- Colossus of Zora.
- Colossus of Regal.
- Colossus of Ashi.

These quests have been corrected to use the appropriate raid quest classification.

This allows the normal AzerothCore quest system to award kill credit while participating in a raid group, rather than relying on additional custom quest-completion handling.

This is particularly important for the Ahn'Qiraj opening event, where players are expected to participate in large groups.

──────────────────────────────────

# Ahn'Qiraj — Twin Emperors

Individual Progression has received an encounter correction for the Twin Emperors in the Temple of Ahn'Qiraj.

The affected boss is:

Emperor Vek'lor

Previously, an incorrect immunity configuration could allow physical attacks and taunt effects to affect Emperor Vek'lor.

This was inconsistent with the intended Twin Emperors encounter mechanics.

──────────────────────────────────

# Emperor Vek'lor — Immunity Restoration

Emperor Vek'lor's intended immunities have been restored.

The changes include:

• Restored immunity to physical damage.

• Restored immunity to taunt effects.

• Corrected the creature immunity configuration.

• Prevented physical attacks and taunts from bypassing the intended encounter mechanics.

This restores the distinction between the Twin Emperors.

Emperor Vek'lor:

Immune to physical damage.

Emperor Vek'nilash:

Immune to magic damage.

These separate immunities are an important part of the encounter's intended design.

The correction helps preserve the requirement for appropriate physical and magical damage roles during the fight.

This correction originated from an Individual Progression upstream update.

──────────────────────────────────

# Desolace — Gizelton Caravan

The Gizelton Caravan in Desolace has received a substantial collection of fixes.

These changes affect the caravan itself and the associated escort quests:

- Bodyguard for Hire.
- Gizelton Caravan.

Improvements include:

- Caravan members now assist each other when attacked.
- Caravan members correctly recognise nearby enemies during escort events.
- Missing dialogue during ambushes has been restored.
- Additional dialogue has been restored when an escort is completed.
- The caravan now walks while an escort quest is active.
- The caravan returns to normal running behaviour outside escort events.
- Caravan stopping and movement behaviour has been corrected.
- The southern vendor stop has received positioning corrections.
- Normal shop-stop duration has been restored to 600 seconds.

These changes should make both escort quests more reliable and restore more of the intended caravan behaviour.

──────────────────────────────────

# Silverpine Forest — Wild Hearts

The Wild Hearts quest has received a scripting improvement.

After turning in the quest to Apothecary Renferrel, the associated completion sequence should now play correctly.

The restored sequence includes:

- Quest-completion dialogue.
- The appropriate NPC animation or emote.
- A return to normal NPC behaviour after the event.

Apothecary Renferrel also retains his questgiver functionality while the sequence takes place.

──────────────────────────────────

# Blackrock Depths — Dark Coffer Event

The Dark Coffer event has received maintenance and compatibility improvements.

Individual Progression previously maintained a separate custom implementation of the Dark Coffer event.

AzerothCore now contains its own implementation, making the older duplicate version unnecessary.

The redundant Individual Progression implementation has therefore been removed.

The Dark Coffer event itself has not been removed from Blackrock Depths.

Instead, the server now relies on the AzerothCore implementation, reducing duplicated scripting and potential conflicts.

──────────────────────────────────

# Zul'Farrak — Patrol Improvements

Individual Progression has received adjustments relating to Zul'Farrak patrol handling.

Some older custom behaviour has been moved back to the newer AzerothCore implementation where appropriate.

This reduces the number of duplicated patrol overrides that Individual Progression needs to maintain.

──────────────────────────────────

# Azuregos

Azuregos has received a boss-scripting improvement.

The change addresses reports that Azuregos could occasionally fail to deal damage correctly during an encounter.

His spell-handling behaviour has been moved into a more conventional event-driven boss script.

The intention is to make his offensive abilities behave more consistently during combat.

──────────────────────────────────

# Twilight Cultist Equipment — Drop Rates

The drop-rate settings for several Twilight Cultist equipment pieces have been reduced.

The affected items are:

- Twilight Cultist Cowl.
- Twilight Cultist Mantle.
- Twilight Cultist Robe.

Each item's configured drop-rate value has been changed from:

8 → 2

The affected enemies are:

- Twilight Avenger.
- Twilight Geolord.
- Twilight Stonecaller.

This adjustment is intended to make acquiring the Twilight Cultist equipment set less immediate and provide a more meaningful progression opportunity in Silithus.

──────────────────────────────────

# Twilight Cultist Enemies — Reputation Rewards

Several Twilight Cultist enemies have received increased reputation rewards when killed.

Twilight Avenger:

Previous: 1 Reputation

New: 2 Reputation

Twilight Geolord:

Remains at 1 Reputation.

Twilight Stonecaller:

Previous: 1 Reputation

New: 2 Reputation

Twilight Geolords intentionally retain their previous reputation reward because of their relatively large population.

──────────────────────────────────

# Dark Iron Tunnelers — Wetlands

Several Dark Iron Tunnelers located in the north-eastern Wetlands have received a creature-data correction.

Previously, some Tunnelers had incorrect flags that prevented their nameplates and health bars from displaying normally.

Those incorrect flags have been removed.

The affected creatures should now display their names and health bars correctly.

──────────────────────────────────

# Green Whelp Armor

Green Whelp Armor has received a correction to restore its intended custom Naxxramas behaviour.

Its Sleep proc can now affect eligible enemies up to:

Level 63

Previously, the standard AzerothCore implementation restricted the proc to enemies up to Level 50.

This restores the usefulness of the item's special effect against appropriate higher-level Vanilla enemies.

# WORLD EVENT UPDATES:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

# Elemental Invasions — Classic World Event

The elemental forces of Azeroth are stirring once again.

Elemental Invasions are a recurring outdoor world event originally introduced during Vanilla World of Warcraft.

During these invasions, mysterious portals from the Elemental Plane appear across several regions of Kalimdor, allowing hostile elemental creatures to enter Azeroth.

Adventurers are encouraged to investigate these disturbances, defeat the invading forces and confront the powerful elemental leaders commanding them.

Four regions are associated with the invasions:

Azshara — Earth Invasion

Thundering Invaders emerge in northeastern Azshara, led by the powerful earth elemental Avalanchion.

Silithus — Air Invasion

Whirling Invaders descend upon northwestern Silithus under the command of The Windreaver.

Un'Goro Crater — Fire Invasion

Blazing Invaders threaten the central regions of Un'Goro Crater, accompanied by their leader, Baron Charr.

Winterspring — Water Invasion

Watery Invaders gather around Lake Kel'Theril, where the formidable Princess Tempestria commands the invasion.

──────────────────────────────────

# Elemental Invasions — Encounters and Rewards

Players can battle invading elemental creatures for valuable materials and seek out the elite leaders for additional rewards.

Depending on the creature and encounter, possible rewards include:

- Elemental crafting materials and essences.
- Rare equipment and accessories.
- Profession patterns.
- The Ace of Elementals, used as part of the Darkmoon Elementals Deck.

While many ordinary elemental invaders can be defeated individually, the powerful invasion leaders are intended to provide a more challenging encounter, making group participation advisable.

The event offers another opportunity for players to explore the original Vanilla world, collect useful materials and pursue rare rewards.

──────────────────────────────────

# Elemental Invasions — Monthly Event Schedule

A new calendar-based scheduling system has been introduced through the Naxxramas Core module.

Instead of relying on fixed recurrence intervals, the event is now configured around the calendar month.

Monthly Schedule

- Begins on the 1st of each month.
- Starts at 00:00 server time.
- Remains active for five full days.
- Ends on the 6th at 00:00 server time.
- Returns automatically the following month.

The system accounts for varying month lengths, including February and leap years.

──────────────────────────────────

# Elemental Invasions — Automatic Event Management

The new scheduling controller is designed to maintain the correct event state without requiring regular manual activation.

When the Worldserver restarts, the system determines whether the current date falls within the scheduled invasion period.

If an invasion should be active, the controller restores the event.

Once the scheduled period has finished, the controller deactivates the event.

The original invasion creatures, encounters and rewards have not been deliberately altered by these scheduling changes.

The module controls the overall event window rather than changing the individual encounters themselves.

──────────────────────────────────

# Another Year, Another Souvenir!

The Brewfest quest Another Year, Another Souvenir! has received additional reward options for both Horde and Alliance characters.

Players can now choose from the available Brewfest stein rewards rather than being limited to the previous reward selection.

For players who already own the available steins, an additional reward option has been introduced:

10 Brewfest Prize Tokens

This allows returning players to continue receiving a useful reward rather than obtaining a duplicate stein they no longer need.

──────────────────────────────────

# Brewfest — Drunkenness Accessibility

A new accessibility option has been added to the Brewfest Ram Racing Apprentices.

Affected NPCs:

Alliance:

Goldark Snipehunter

Horde:

Glodrak Huntsniper

Players can now select the following dialogue option:

"The drinking effects are making me feel unwell. Could you sober me up?"

Selecting this option immediately removes normal drunkenness effects.

It also removes simulated drunkenness effects, including effects associated with items such as Synthebrew Goggles.

This provides an accessibility option for players who find the drunken visual effects uncomfortable.

The existing Brewfest dialogue and Synthebrew Goggles functionality remain available.

There is no Gold cost or special configuration requirement for this accessibility feature.

# CLASSIC MEETING STONES:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

# Classic Meeting Stones — Trial Feature

A new experimental Meeting Stone system has been developed to better reflect the original Vanilla experience.

During original Vanilla progression, Meeting Stones did not provide the same player-summoning functionality introduced in later expansions.

The new system aims to restore that distinction while maintaining compatibility with Individual Progression.

──────────────────────────────────

# Meeting Stones — Vanilla Progression

During Vanilla progression, Meeting Stones will remain present throughout the world.

However, their summoning functionality is restricted.

Players interacting with a Meeting Stone will receive a message explaining that player summoning becomes available upon reaching The Burning Crusade.

During Vanilla progression:

• Meeting Stones remain visible and accessible.

• Meeting Stones cannot be used to summon other players.

• Players receive an explanation when attempting to use the restricted summoning functionality.

This encourages players to travel to dungeon entrances rather than relying on later-expansion summoning mechanics.

──────────────────────────────────

# Meeting Stones — Burning Crusade & Wrath

Meeting Stone summoning becomes available normally when players reach the appropriate expansion progression.

During The Burning Crusade and Wrath of the Lich King:

• Meeting Stones can be used for normal player summoning.

• Existing group requirements remain unchanged.

• Existing level restrictions remain unchanged.

• Normal summoning requirements continue to apply.

The system checks each character's Individual Progression stage rather than applying one global expansion restriction to every player.

──────────────────────────────────

# Meeting Stones — Trial Status

Classic Meeting Stones is being introduced as an experimental feature.

Its impact on dungeon accessibility, group formation and player convenience will be evaluated before deciding whether to retain it permanently.

The system is independently configurable.

If disabled, normal Meeting Stone summoning functionality is restored without affecting other Naxxramas Core systems.

Status:

Experimental feature requiring server compilation, deployment and testing.

# PVP & HONOR SYSTEMS:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

# Forced PvP Zones

A new Forced PvP Zone system has been introduced.

The following zones now support forced faction PvP:

- Silithus.
- Eastern Plaguelands.

While the system is enabled for a zone, Alliance and Horde players are automatically placed into normal faction PvP when entering.

Players cannot manually disable their PvP flag while remaining within a forced PvP zone.

The system remembers the player's previous PvP preference.

When leaving:

- Players who were already manually PvP flagged remain flagged.
- Players who were previously unflagged can return to their normal PvP-off state after the standard cooldown.
- Game Masters are excluded.
- Playerbots are supported.

Both zones can be configured independently or disabled entirely through Naxxramas Core.

An optional entry notification is also supported.

──────────────────────────────────

# Honor Overflow — New System

A new Honor Overflow system has been introduced.

Previously, Honor earned after reaching the server's maximum Honor currency limit could be wasted.

Honor Overflow changes this behaviour.

Once a player reaches the configured Honor cap, additional genuinely earned Honor is converted into currency.

The default conversion rate is:

100 Honor = 10 Silver

1,000 Honor = 1 Gold

The system only converts Honor that exceeds the cap.

Example:

A player currently has:

74,900 Honor

They earn:

250 Honor

If the configured Honor cap is 75,000:

- 100 Honor is added to their spendable Honor.
- The remaining 150 Honor is converted.
- The player receives 15 Silver.

Players also receive an in-game notification explaining the conversion.

Additional safeguards include:

- Uses AzerothCore's configured Honor cap.
- Does not count direct GM Honor modifications.
- Protects against exceeding the character Gold cap.
- Excludes Playerbots by default.
- Can be enabled, disabled or adjusted through configuration.

Battleground Honor Overflow notifications have also been improved to provide a summary rather than flooding the chat window with repeated messages.

──────────────────────────────────

# Fortnightly Honor Reset

A new automatic Honor-reset system has been introduced through Naxxramas Core.

Spendable Honor is scheduled to reset every two weeks.

Configured schedule:

Every second Wednesday at 06:00 server time.

The reset is designed to affect both online and offline characters.

Only spendable Honor is reset.

The following remain intact:

- Lifetime Honorable Kills.
- PvP achievements.
- Earned titles.
- Existing PvP statistics unrelated to spendable Honor.

The reset system also includes restart-safe scheduling.

If the server is offline when a reset is due, the system can process the missed scheduled reset when the server next starts.

The last completed reset is recorded to help prevent duplicate executions.

──────────────────────────────────

# Fortnightly Honor Reset — Reliability Correction

A problem was identified during the first scheduled Honor reset.

Although the database recorded the reset as processed, some characters who had been offline retained their existing Honor balances.

The reset implementation has now been corrected to use an appropriate synchronous database operation for the bulk Honor update.

The existing schedule has been preserved.

The missed reset has not been automatically repeated, preventing Honor earned after the original reset date from being immediately removed.

The existing schedule remains every second Wednesday at 06:00 server time.

Status:

Correction committed. Successful operation for both online and offline characters still requires verification during the next scheduled reset.

──────────────────────────────────

# PvP Titles — Individual Progression

Individual Progression has received an optional configuration setting allowing players to retain all PvP rank titles they have earned.

Previously, the progression system normally retained only the highest earned PvP rank title.

The new option allows a server to let players continue selecting previously earned lower-rank titles.

This functionality is configurable and depends on the server's chosen setting.

# CLASSIC BATTLEGROUND QUEUEING:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

# Classic Battleground Queueing

A new expansion-aware Battleground queueing system has been developed.

The purpose of this system is to encourage players to visit Battlemaster NPCs during Vanilla and Burning Crusade progression, restoring a more authentic earlier-expansion experience.

Rather than allowing every character to use the Wrath of the Lich King remote Battleground interface, availability can now depend on their Individual Progression stage.

──────────────────────────────────

# Battleground Queueing — Vanilla

During Vanilla progression, players are expected to visit a Battlemaster NPC to enter Battleground queues when the restriction is enabled.

The intended behaviour is:

• Battlemaster NPCs remain available in their existing locations.

• Players can queue through the appropriate Battlemaster.

• Remote Battleground queueing is restricted.

• Attempts to bypass the restriction using remote queue commands are checked by the server.

This is intended to restore the importance of Battlemaster NPCs during Vanilla progression.

──────────────────────────────────

# Battleground Queueing — The Burning Crusade

During The Burning Crusade progression, the same Battlemaster requirement remains in place when the restriction is enabled.

Players continue using Battlemaster NPCs to join Battleground queues.

Remote Battleground queueing remains restricted.

Arena functionality is handled separately and is not intended to be removed by the Battleground queue restrictions.

──────────────────────────────────

# Battleground Queueing — Wrath of the Lich King

Upon reaching Individual Progression Stage 13, the normal Wrath of the Lich King remote Battleground queueing functionality becomes available.

Players can then access Battleground queues using the standard remote interface.

This restores the later-expansion convenience at the intended progression stage.

──────────────────────────────────

# Battleground Queueing — Compatibility

Additional safeguards have been introduced for groups containing players at different Individual Progression stages.

The system also includes configurable exemptions for:

• Game Masters.

• Playerbots.

This helps preserve compatibility with the server's existing automated character systems.

──────────────────────────────────

# Battleground Queueing — Configuration

The server-side Battleground queue restriction is optional.

Default state:

Disabled.

The system will remain disabled by default until compilation and testing have been completed.

This means the existing Battleground queueing behaviour is preserved unless the new restriction is explicitly enabled.

The restriction can be configured independently of the new Battleground interface addon.

# GENERAL GAMEPLAY & QUALITY-OF-LIFE:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

# Same-Account Mail Delivery

Mail sent between characters belonging to the same account now respects the server's normal mail-delivery delay.

Previously, mail sent between a player's own characters could arrive instantly.

This has been changed.

Current server delivery time:

1 hour

This brings same-account mail back in line with the configured mail-delivery rules.

Exceptions remain for:

- Returned mail.
- COD payment mail.
- GM and customer-support mail.
- System-generated mail.

These retain their existing delivery behaviour.

──────────────────────────────────

# Trainer Spell Restrictions

AzerothCore has received a correction to trainer spell handling.

Some trainer entries teach abilities by casting another spell rather than directly learning one.

Previously, Individual Progression could block the restricted ability while secondary effects from the trainer action still occurred.

For example, a restricted class mount could fail to be learned while still granting part of the associated Riding skill.

The updated system checks the relevant spell-learning restrictions before the complete trainer action is executed.

This improves consistency when expansion-specific spells or abilities are restricted.

──────────────────────────────────

# Persistent Area-of-Effect Spells

A persistent spell-effect issue has been corrected.

Some Warlock, Mage and Hunter area-of-effect spells could incorrectly remain active after combat ended.

Additional cleanup handling has been restored to prevent these effects from persisting when they should have ended.

──────────────────────────────────

# In-Game Calendar

The in-game calendar has received a correction relating to disabled world events and holidays.

Previously, disabling certain holidays could cause the calendar to report an incorrect number of holiday records.

This has been corrected so the calendar reports only the holiday information actually sent to the client.

This improves compatibility with the server's customised event configuration.

# PLAYERBOT UPDATES:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

# Playerbot Equipment Evaluation

Playerbots have received improvements to how they evaluate equipment upgrades.

The equipment scoring system now places greater emphasis on the actual stats provided by an item.

Changes include:

- Item Level is no longer unnecessarily multiplied into an item's score.
- Item quality is no longer treated as an additional score multiplier.
- The previous heavy Resilience penalty has been removed.
- Feral Druid weapons are evaluated more accurately.
- Feral weapon Attack Power is recognised correctly.
- Classes that do not benefit from Feral-only bonuses should no longer incorrectly value them.

This should help Playerbots select equipment based on its usefulness to their role and specialization.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Gem Socketing

Automatic gem socketing has received an improvement.

Playerbots will now avoid socketing a gem whose quality is higher than the quality of the equipment receiving it.

This reduces unnecessary use of valuable gems on lower-quality or temporary equipment.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Blackwing Lair Improvements

Playerbots have received additional boss-specific combat improvements for Blackwing Lair.

The changes focus on improved positioning, target priorities and avoidance of unnecessary damage.

Broodlord Lashlayer:

- Ranged bots attempt to maintain a safer distance from Broodlord.
- Tank bots are less likely to abandon Broodlord to attack nearby Corrupted Whelps.

Firemaw, Ebonroc and Flamegor:

- Non-tank bots caught in frontal attack areas attempt to reposition.
- Bots try to move towards safer side or rear positions.
- Tanks continue maintaining the boss's intended position.

Nefarian:

- Non-tank bots attempt to position around Nefarian's rear flank.
- This reduces exposure to frontal abilities such as Cleave and Shadow Flame while avoiding his Tail Lash.

Death Talon Wyrmguards:

- Improved ranged positioning.
- Bots currently tanking a Wyrmguard should no longer attempt unnecessary kiting.

These improvements are intended to improve the reliability of Playerbot-assisted Blackwing Lair raids.

They do not change the server's existing raid unlock requirements.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Fear Ward Behaviour

Older raid-specific Fear Ward handling has been cleaned up.

Priest bots can now rely more consistently on their existing Fear Ward behaviour when supporting the group's main tank.

Additional encounter-specific fear handling has also been adjusted for later content, including the Wizard of Oz Opera encounter in Karazhan.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Battleground Resurrection

An issue involving repeated Playerbot deaths in battlegrounds has been corrected.

Previously, bots could eventually attempt normal open-world corpse recovery rather than remaining within the battleground resurrection system.

This could result in bots being sent to an outside graveyard or leaving the battleground incorrectly.

Battleground deaths should now remain within the battleground's intended resurrection flow.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Arena Team Improvements

Playerbot arena-team assignment and management logic has received corrections.

These changes are intended to improve how automated characters are assigned to and managed within arena teams.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Command — Target Me

A new Playerbot command has been added:

`target me`

This instructs a Playerbot to target the player who issued the command.

The command is useful for abilities and interactions that require a particular friendly player to be selected.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Spell Tome Learning

Playerbots can now use spell-learning consumable items more reliably.

Affected item types include:

- Codices.
- Manuals.
- Tomes.
- Similar spell-learning consumables.

This corrects cases where an ability's targeting requirements previously interfered with learning it from the corresponding item.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Quest Item Looting

Playerbots have received improvements to their recognition of quest-related items.

Items such as quest keys may now be recognised as useful even when they are not directly listed as a normal quest objective.

This should reduce situations where a bot ignores an item required for quest or dungeon progression.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Locked Chest Handling

Playerbots can now use physical keys to open eligible locked chests more reliably.

The system uses the key's own unlocking spell, matching the normal client behaviour more closely.

Additional fixes prevent item-target handling from incorrectly redirecting lockbox or trade-window unlocking actions towards a nearby world object.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Gathering Improvements

An issue has been corrected where Playerbots with heavily filled inventories could repeatedly attempt to gather the same Herb or Mining node.

This could cause a bot to become stuck in a continuous gathering loop without successfully collecting anything.

The updated handling prevents this repeated failed interaction.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Consumable Notifications

A new Playerbot configuration option has been introduced:

`AiPlayerbot.AnnounceConsumableUse`

This setting can be used to suppress repeated consumable-related whispers such as:

- Eating...
- Drinking...
- Feasting...

Disabling the announcements does not disable the bot's actual food or drink behaviour.

──────────────────────────────────

# Playerbot Class Selection

The `.playerbots bot addclass` system has received an optional random-selection mode.

Previously, removing and re-adding a bot of a particular class could repeatedly select the same eligible character.

Dungeon Clear has received a significant improvement to tank and party combat coordination.

Previously, damage-dealing Playerbots could sometimes begin attacking before the tank had established sufficient threat.

The updated system now tracks when the tank successfully begins engaging an enemy.

Damage-dealing bots then respect the configured threat-building delay.

This protection applies to:

- Normal damage rotations.
- Direct damaging abilities.
- Damaging area-of-effect abilities.
- Newly engaged enemy groups.

Additional safeguards ensure:

- Healing remains available during the delay.
- Party members under attack can respond when required.

# AzerothCore — Creature Performance

AzerothCore has received improvements to creature movement and script lookup performance.

Two particularly expensive operations have been optimised:

- Terrain-status calculations for moving creatures.
- Repeated creature Script ID lookups.

Creature terrain information can now be calculated when required rather than repeatedly performing unnecessary calculations.

Creature Script ID lookups are also cached where appropriate.

In upstream testing, these changes reduced CPU usage and average idle update times.

Actual results will vary according to server hardware, world activity and Playerbot population.

──────────────────────────────────

# AzerothCore — Follower & Summon Stability

A crash involving units with follower movement has been corrected.

The issue could occur when a unit was destroyed without all follower references being properly cleared.

Affected systems could include:

- Pets.
- Guardians.
- Totems.
- Temporary summons.
- Other follower-controlled units.

Follower cleanup is now also performed during unit destruction to prevent stale references and potential crashes.

# AzerothCore — Headless Playerbot Sessions

The AzerothCore and Playerbots integration has received architectural updates.

Playerbots now makes greater use of AzerothCore's headless-session support rather than relying on older modifications intended to make bots behave like ordinary network-connected players.

Additional session-independent APIs and scripting hooks have been introduced.

These changes are intended to improve long-term compatibility between AzerothCore and Playerbots.

# Individual Progression — Damage Scaling

Individual Progression has received an important correction involving self-inflicted and friendly damage.

Previously, certain damage mechanics could be reduced by the module's progression scaling even though the damage was not normal hostile damage.

Affected situations included:

- Self-inflicted damage.
- Friendly party damage.
- Mind-controlled players attacking allies.
- Mechanics implemented internally as friendly or self damage.

Examples include interactions involving:

- Shadow Word: Death.
- Dark and Demonic Runes.
- Vaelastrasz's Burning Adrenaline.
- Gruul's Shatter.
- Flame Wreath.
- Burning Crusade raid mechanics.
- Mind-control mechanics.

The new handling prevents progression damage reductions from unintentionally reducing these types of damage.

This is intended to preserve the difficulty and functionality of encounters that rely on them.

# Dungeon Clear — Multithreaded Stability

Dungeon Clear has received a thread-safety fix affecting:

`BossSpawnIndex`

and:

`DungeonSpawnGraph`

Previously, multiple map-update threads could attempt to initialise these internal caches at the same time.

This could result in incomplete data being accessed or concurrent modifications causing instability.

Both caches now use one-time initialisation safeguards.

This ensures a single thread performs the initial construction while other threads wait for completion.

The change is particularly important on servers with multiple map-update threads and large Playerbot populations.

# Dungeon Clear — Pull Lab

- Damage-dealer attack timing.
- Unexpected enemy aggression.
- Patrol interruptions.

Available commands include:

- `.dc lab show`
- `.dc lab run`
- `.dc lab batch`
- `.dc lab status`
- `.dc lab stop`

Pull Lab is intended for development and troubleshooting rather than altering ordinary dungeon gameplay.
